title: Tenant Configuration
brief:
As a platform admin, I want each tenant to be able to customize its feature flags and limits, so that tenants can differ from the organization defaults where they need to.

Acceptance criteria:
- A tenant that sets no value of its own gets the organization default for it.
- A tenant's own value replaces the default, for each flag and each limit separately.
- An operation that would take a tenant over one of its limits is rejected (429) and does not run.
- An operation that adds several items at once is rejected unless all of them fit.

steps.summary: Add the tenant feature-flag and limit types plus the organization defaults
Merge the organization defaults with each tenant's overrides
Add the 429 quota error and the usage checks that wrap an operation
Add tests for config merging and quota checks, document the model

probes.question: What is the organization default for maxUsers?
A tenant overrides only { features: { refunds: false } }. Is analytics enabled for it?
A tenant with maxUsers 5 already has 4 users. withQuota is called to add 3 users at once (amount 3). What happens?

items.question: A tenant overrides its limits with { maxUsers: null }. What is its effective maxUsers limit?
A tenant's overrides contain a limit the platform does not have: { limits: { maxWidgets: 3 } }. What happens to it?
options: It is dropped: the effective limits are only the known ones
It is kept in the effective limits
Resolving the configuration rejects it as invalid

items.question: A tenant has overridden maxProducts with null and already has 100 products; the organization default is 100. It adds 1 product through withQuota. What happens?
options: It runs: the tenant has no limit

items.question: A tenant with a maxProducts limit of 100 has 98 products and imports 5 at once through withQuota. What happens?
options: The import is rejected: quota exceeded (429)
The import is rejected as invalid (400)

items.question: A tenant overrides its limits with { maxUsers: 0 } and has no users yet. It adds one user through withQuota. What happens?
options: It runs: 0 counts as not set, so the default of 5 applies
